questions: Check signatory adoption, contract revision races and invalidation of completed tasks.
Bound registry loading and evidence required to reopen a consumer.
decision: Strengthen versioned shared patterns with compare-and-swap updates and selective consumer invalidation, without building a global context dump.
code_observations: patternctl already represents explicit signatories and pattern revisions; pattern_runner_contract integrates them into execution.
Shared normative patterns and runtime learnings are different contracts. Reopening every completed task would erase the selectivity the existing mechanism is intended to provide.
implementation_steps: Require the updater to provide the observed revision/digest and reject a stale writer rather than silently overwriting a newer contract.
Bind each consumer acceptance to the exact pattern revision. A revision change reopens only completed signatories that used an older revision; pending consumers just read the new revision.
Record a concise change rationale and migration impact. Avoid copying whole prior pattern histories into worker prompts.
Serialize writes for shared pattern files or use a tested lock/atomic write seam. Do not claim atomicity across independent files without recovery tests.
Limit registry lookup to assigned pattern IDs and make adoption evidence part of deterministic validation.
proposed_acceptance_tests: Two writers using the same starting revision cannot both silently succeed.
An unaffected completed task remains completed after an unrelated pattern change.
A stale completed signatory is reopened exactly once with a reason.
Malformed or escaping pattern paths cannot be read or deleted.
A worker receives only assigned current contracts, not the entire registry/history.

alternatives.title: Last writer wins and broad reopening
alternatives.tradeoff: Simple, but races and excessive rework undermine durable progress.

alternatives.title: Revision-aware updates and selective invalidation
alternatives.tradeoff: Small deterministic bookkeeping with bounded revalidation.

alternatives.title: Duplicate the same contract in every task
alternatives.tradeoff: Copies drift and increase tokens while obscuring the authoritative version.

cost_model: Compare number of invalidated tasks, bytes loaded and repeated validations. Preserve the current simple file-backed design unless measured contention justifies another store.
unverified: Cross-host concurrent execution requires an explicit storage/locking contract; local filesystem tests cannot establish distributed locking.
runtime_experiments: No authenticated model calls; tests listed here are implementation obligations, not claimed passes.
